get.description: Returns a single embedding from a collection, looked up by its UUID.

put.description: Replaces the vector and/or metadata of an existing embedding, looked up by its UUID. A new vector must match the collection's dimensions.

delete.description: Permanently deletes a single embedding from a collection, looked up by its UUID. This cannot be undone.

put.summary: Create or update embeddings in collection
put.description:
Creates one or more embeddings in a collection, replacing any that already exist with the same UUID. Every vector must match the collection's dimensions.

Authorization is resolved per request:

- If `authz` is set on the request body, that path is applied to all embeddings in the request.
- Otherwise the collection's own path, `/vectorstore/collections/{collection_name}`, is used.
- You need both `create` and `update` permission on the collection path and on the resulting embedding paths.

get.description: Returns the embeddings in a collection, one page at a time. Set `exclude_info=true` to omit the `info` block from each result.

post.description:
Creates one or more embeddings in a collection. Every vector must match the collection's dimensions. Use `PUT` on this path instead if you want existing embeddings to be replaced rather than rejected.

Authorization is resolved per request:

- If `authz` is set on the request body, those paths are applied to all embeddings in the request.
- Otherwise the collection's own path, `/vectorstore/collections/{collection_name}`, is used.
- You need `create` permission on the collection path and on the resulting embedding paths.

post.summary: Read select embeddings from unknown collections
post.description:
Returns the requested embeddings by UUID without needing to know which collection each one belongs to, along with the metadata for every collection involved. Vectors are returned in a binary encoding. UUIDs that do not resolve are omitted from the response rather than raising an error.

This uses `POST` so the UUID list can be sent in the request body, but it does not create anything.

Returns the requested embeddings by UUID from a single known collection. Vectors are returned in a binary encoding. UUIDs that do not resolve within the collection are omitted from the response rather than raising an error.

This uses `POST` so the UUID list can be sent in the request body, but it does not create anything.

get.description: Returns every vector collection you have access to, one page at a time. Set `counts=true` to also get the number of embeddings available in each collection.

post.description: Creates a new vector collection. The collection name is normalized before it is stored, and the dimensions you supply here are enforced on every embedding added to the collection.

get.description: Returns the metadata for a single collection, including its dimensions and vector type. Set `counts=true` to also get the number of embeddings available in it.

patch.description: Updates the mutable metadata on a collection, such as its description. The collection's name, dimensions, and vector type cannot be changed after creation.

delete.description: Permanently deletes a collection and every embedding stored in it. This cannot be undone.

post.description: Finds the embeddings in a collection nearest to the query vector you provide, ordered by similarity. The query vector must have the same number of dimensions as the collection. Set `exclude_info=true` to omit the `info` block from each result.

Finds the embeddings nearest to the query vector across every collection you have access to, ordered by similarity. Pass a comma-separated `collections` list to restrict the search to specific collections. Only collections matching the requested `vector_type` and the query vector's dimensions are searched.

EmbeddingToCreate.title: EmbeddingToCreate
EmbeddingToCreate.description:
Data for creating a single embedding in a collection.

'embedding' can be:
  - list[float] (already-embedded vector)
  - list[str]   (text chunks to be embedded later, not yet implemented here)

For now, our code will only accept list[float] until we wire in the AI model
service for text → embedding.
